subject: science

sections.scope_note: Arizona standards deferred. This crosswalk covers Florida NGSSS Science (2016) and IB PYP only. Rows are suggested (Label C).

ib_framework_elements: PYP transdisciplinary theme: How the world works
rows.key_differences: Florida's six benchmarks specify variables, a control group, repeated trials, the difference between an experiment and other investigations, and opinion versus verified observation. Public PYP text describes inquiry without those six sentences.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Plan a short experiment with one variable and a control, repeat it, and separate what was observed from what was inferred.

ib_framework_elements: PYP learner profile: Inquirers (name reused from grade 3)
rows.key_differences: Florida requires that explanations link to testable evidence and that evidence should be replicable. Those sentences are NGSSS, not published PYP phase outcomes.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: When a claim comes up in the inquiry, ask what evidence would let someone else check it.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Science: Forces and energy (strand name reused from grade 3)
PYP transdisciplinary theme: How the world works
rows.key_differences: Florida lists forms of energy, charged objects, energy transformations, closed circuits, conductors, and how force and mass affect motion, including balanced forces. The strand name is reused; the investigations are Florida's.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Test a closed circuit and one push or pull, and name the form of energy that changes.

rows.topic_domain: Living things - organs, change, and adaptations
ib_framework_elements: PYP Science: Living things (strand name reused from grade 3)
PYP transdisciplinary theme: Sharing the planet
PYP concept: Change (name reused from grade 3)
rows.key_differences: Florida names human organs, compares plant and animal support structures, and describes survival when the environment changes. Sharing the planet is a public theme; the organ list is Florida's.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Compare one structure that supports a plant and one that supports an animal, then ask which differences would matter if the environment changed.

rows.topic_domain: Earth in space and Earth systems
ib_framework_elements: PYP Science: Earth and space (strand name reused from grade 3)
PYP concept: Change (name reused from grade 3)
PYP concept: Responsibility (name reused from grade 3)
rows.key_differences: Florida covers galaxies and the Solar System, the water cycle and ocean, weather variables, forms of precipitation, climate zones, and a family natural-disaster plan. The public pages do not list those models.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Model one part of the water cycle and connect a local weather observation to why a family might plan for a natural disaster.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Science: Materials and matter (strand name reused from grade 3)
PYP concept: Form (name reused from grade 3)
PYP concept: Change (name reused from grade 3)
rows.key_differences: Florida compares solids, liquids, and gases, investigates dissolving, separates mixtures by observable properties, recognizes that matter is made of parts too small to see, and links physical and chemical changes to temperature. The strand name is reused, not a grade 5 IB outcome.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Separate a mixture by an observable property, then change the temperature and record what changed.

version_notes: 2026-10-03: Grade 5 FL↔IB crosswalk. Arizona left empty (deferred). Rows are suggested alignments (Label C). Florida IDs are from the grade 5 drafts. IB elements are either public PYP framework text or the same strand labels used in the grade 2 and grade 3 crosswalks. No IB learning outcomes were invented.
